name: fix_sql_null_comparison
description: Fixes three-valued-logic filtering that drops NULL-status rows
prompts: query.sql should return every task that is NOT done - including tasks whose status is NULL (never started). But `status != 'done'` uses SQL three-valued logic: for NULL status it evaluates to NULL, not TRUE, so those rows are dropped. Fix query.sql so NULL-status tasks are included (IS NULL OR, COALESCE, or IS DISTINCT FROM - any correct idiom). Table: tasks(id, title, status). Keep the columns and ORDER BY id.

setup_files.query.sql:
-- All tasks that are not yet done.
-- BUG: `status != 'done'` is NULL (not TRUE) for rows with NULL status,
-- so unstarted tasks silently disappear from the result.
SELECT id, title, status
FROM tasks
WHERE status != 'done'
ORDER BY id;

test_setup_files.test_query.py:
import sqlite3

conn = sqlite3.connect(':memory:')
conn.executescript('''
CREATE TABLE tasks (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT, status TEXT);
INSERT INTO tasks (id, title, status) VALUES
    (1, 'ship', 'done'),
    (2, 'test', 'in_progress'),
    (3, 'plan', NULL),
    (4, 'review', 'todo'),
    (5, 'retire', 'done');
''')
rows = [tuple(r) for r in conn.execute(open('query.sql').read()).fetchall()]
assert rows == [(2, 'test', 'in_progress'), (3, 'plan', None), (4, 'review', 'todo')], \
    f'NULL-status tasks must be included: {rows}'
print('PASS')

reference_solution.query.sql:
SELECT id, title, status
FROM tasks
WHERE status IS NULL OR status != 'done'
ORDER BY id;

files.query.sql:
SELECT id, title, status
FROM tasks
WHERE status IS NULL OR status != 'in_progress'
ORDER BY id;
